bando.titolo: New European Bauhaus Prizes — Rising Stars
bando.sottotitolo: Strand B — for talents aged 30 or under
bando.descrizione: Ideas that make Europe more beautiful, sustainable and inclusive. Concepts can be at any stage, from a clear plan to a working prototype. Applications are submitted in English.

categorie.nome: Arts, culture and heritage as drivers of change

descrizioneLunga: The New European Bauhaus is the European Commission's attempt to make the green transition **something people actually want to live in** — not only efficient, but beautiful and shared. The Prizes reward the projects that show what that means in practice.

**Strand B is reserved for you.** Every listed author must be __30 years old or younger__ on the closing day. You are not competing against architecture firms or city councils: you compete against other young people with an idea.

An entry does not have to be a finished thing. Concepts are accepted __at any stage of development__ — from a clear plan on paper to a working prototype. What the jury looks for is whether the idea is **sustainable, beautiful and inclusive at the same time**: two out of three is not enough, and that is the hardest part.

Applications are submitted **in English**, on the official platform. Winning brings €15,000, but also a communication package from the Commission, a coaching and mentoring programme, and a __public vote across Europe__ that puts the project in front of thousands of people.

One practical note for this alliance: the ERUA rule that a team must span **at least two universities** is not required here — but a cross-border team is exactly what tends to win, because the New European Bauhaus is about places, and Europe has many of them.

vincitori.sintesi: Turns ordinary urban signage into habitats for pollinators — the same poles and panels a city already owns, redesigned to host insects.
Students and residents co-designed a shared courtyard, built out of recycled construction material from the neighbourhood itself.
Farming practices that rebuild soil and biodiversity instead of depleting them, gathered into one place people can learn from.
A research residency held inside a cornfield, putting architects and farmers in the same place to think about design that centres life.
Water read as public space: how a city can use it for climate resilience and as somewhere people gather, at the same time.

squadre.sintesi: Eight campuses throw away the same chairs, lamps and lab stools every June, and buy them again in September. We are mapping what leaves each building and building a shared board where it finds a second owner across the alliance.
squadre.cerca: Someone who can build a simple web catalogue, and one person per campus to do the counting.

squadre.sintesi: A portable wooden structure that sits in a town square for a week and records what residents actually want from the university next door. Built once, shipped between four cities, transcribed and published openly.
squadre.cerca: A carpenter or product designer, and someone comfortable with audio editing.

squadre.sintesi: Student housing built in the 1960s is being demolished across Europe without anyone photographing it. We document four buildings before they go, with the people who lived in them, and turn it into a travelling exhibition.
squadre.cerca: A photographer, and someone who can handle archive permissions.

squadre.sintesi: Every student project starts from zero: the same budget template, the same permission letters, the same mistakes. We are collecting what previous funded teams actually used and releasing it as an open toolkit anyone in Europe can copy.
squadre.cerca: Someone who has already run a funded project, and a translator for at least one more language.

soli.testo: I map seagrass loss around the islands for my thesis. I would like to turn a dataset into something people can actually look at.
I care about how public space makes people feel. I can interview, write and record — I cannot build anything.
I write code for a living and I want to do it once for something that is not a company. Happy to be the only technical person on a team.
I have a camera and two years of editing behind me. Looking for a subject worth six months.
I run a repair café on campus every second Thursday. I would like to make it something more than a hobby.
First year of my master's. I draw well and I know the Aegean islands better than most. Looking for people who need a place to start from.
I can read a call for proposals and tell you what it actually asks for. That is not glamorous but it is why applications fail.
I scan objects in the university museum. I have the equipment and nobody to point it at outside the syllabus.
Older than most here. I have run two association budgets and I know where money disappears. Looking for a team that already has an idea.
I build small devices that record and play back. No idea what for yet — that is why I am here.
I study what mass tourism does to small towns. I would like to work with someone from a place that has the same problem for different reasons.
I can present a project to a room of people who do not care yet. Every team needs one of those.
